s: He’s promised to bring along cake.
to expect (something positive); to hope for
I expect a lot from it.
Er hatte sich einer Frau versprochen und heiratete dann eine andere.
He had promised himself to one woman and then married another.
to make a verbal slip; to misspeak
Entschuldigung, ich habe mich versprochen. Ich meinte „hundert“, nicht „tausend“.
Sorry, I misspoke. I meant “a hundred”, not “a thousand”.
versprechen.et: From Middle High German versprechen (“to guarantee”), from Old High German firsprehhan (“to defend verbally, to warrant”), from Proto-West Germanic *frasprekan. Analyzable as ver- + sprechen. The sense “to misspeak” is a later transparent derivation (see the p…

s: to make fun of, to mock
slip of the tongue (mistake in speech)
to eat up, especially with great pleasure and enjoyment
Die Gäste hatten im Nu den leckeren Puter verspeist.
The guests had eaten up the tasty roast turkey in nothing flat.
to be late, to be delayed
Der Zug verspätet sich um eine Stunde.
The train is delayed an hour.
to gamble something away (lose something in a game)
Spielsüchtige verspielen oft an einem Tag ganze Monatslöhne.
Compulsive gamblers often gamble away entire monthly wages in one day.
to lose something lightly; to squander; to waste
Er hat sein ganzes Erbe mit teuren Partys verspielt.
He squandered his whole inheritance on expensive parties.
Durch den Einmarsch in Afghanistan verspielten die USA leichtfertig ihre moralische Vorteilslage.
By invading Afghanistan the US lightly wasted its moral high ground.
He is out of favour with her.
to make a mistake at playing (e.g. play a wrong note on a music instrument)
An dieser Stelle verspiele ich mich immer.
I always play it wrong at this point.
verspielen.et: From Middle High German verspiln. Analyzable as ver- + spielen. In the sense of “to squander” reinforced by and merged with unrelated Middle Low German verspillen, verspilden (“to waste”). Compare Dutch verspillen.

s: playful, frisky, coltish, sportive, cheerful, prankish
Many plastics embrittle when exposed directly to the sun.
Die Verbindungshaltbarkeit ist begrenzt, weil der Kleber mit der Zeit die Kunststoffbauteile versprödet.
The durability of the joint is limited because over time the glue will embrittle the plastic components.
the destruction, defilement or disruption of natural landscapes through the construction of wind farms
Verspargelung.et: ver- + Spargel (“asparagus”) + -ung, literally “asparagus-ification”, as a comparison of the tall, cylindrical appearance of wind turbines and asparagus and in allusion to the image that wind turbines stick out of the ground like unwanted asparagus.

s: agent noun of verspeisen: Someone who eats something up
agent noun of verspotten; mocker: One who makes fun of someone or something
agent noun of verspielen: One who gambles something away
agent noun of versperren: One who bars or blocks something
agent noun of verspröden: One who, or that which, makes something brittle
to spurt, to squirt, to splash, to spatter, to spray
Sie verspritzt Wasser auf die Pflanzen.
She's spraying water onto the plants.
to verbalize, to turn into language
